project_scope.note: Built to teach sheathing leaves + jointed nodes before flower-level genus differences.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at the node: soft jointed stems and alternate parallel-veined leaves with a conspicuous sheathing base.
family_diagnostics.flower: 3 sepals + 3 petals; stamens may all be fertile or split into fertile stamens and staminodes.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Grass-like leaves are not enough; the sheathing node and 3+3 flower plan are the confirmation.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: The family becomes obvious once you notice the fleshy jointed stem and leaf sheath—then the three-petal flowers make sense.

steps.title: 1 · See the dayflower flower
steps.look_for: Two huge blue petals, one tiny lower petal, and a strongly bilateral flower.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows how far the family can depart from a symmetrical three-petal spiderwort.

steps.title: 2 · Inspect reproductive differentiation
steps.look_for: Three fertile stamens plus three staminodes.

steps.title: 3 · Start vegetatively at the node
steps.look_for: Alternate parallel-veined leaf with its base wrapping the soft jointed stem.
steps.why_it_matters: This separates a vegetative Commelinaceae from many grass-like plants.

steps.title: 4 · Follow to the capsule
steps.look_for: A superior ovary maturing into a loculicidal capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit confirms the monocot flower plan.

comparisons.title: Commelinaceae vs Poaceae
comparisons.rule: Commelinaceae has a sheathing fleshy node and 3-sepal/3-petal flower; Poaceae has a ligule and spikelets with glumes/lemma/palea.

comparisons.title: Commelinaceae vs Iridaceae
comparisons.rule: Iridaceae often has 6 similar tepals and an inferior ovary; Commelinaceae has distinct 3 sepals + 3 petals and a superior ovary.

visual_lesson.caveat: Petals are short-lived and may wilt quickly, so vegetative nodes and fruit are important.
